intro: Lesson 27: Selection and loops core: if, while and for. To understand how selection and repetition control the flow of a Python program

questions.q: Trace the while loop on the slide: write total after each pass.
questions.a: 30, 60, 90, 120; then 120 < 100 is False, so it stops and prints 120.

questions.q: Which loop suits 'keep asking until the password is correct'?
Pupil PDF: write a program that prints the 7 times table (7 × 1 to 7 × 12) with a for loop, then a version that keeps asking for a number until it is between 1 and 12.
questions.a: for i in range(1, 13): print(7, 'x', i, '=', 7 * i); while loop: n = int(input()) repeated while n < 1 or n > 12.
questions.model: The teacher writes the first line: for i in range(1, 13):

questions.q: Extend: use elif to output 'Fizz' for multiples of 3 in 1 to 15.
questions.a: for i in range(1, 16): if i % 3 == 0: print('Fizz') else: print(i)

questions.q: Stretch: when is a while loop dangerous?
questions.a: If the condition never becomes False: an infinite loop.

questions.q: Which keyword gives a second condition after if?
Back to our ponder: A teacher calls the register: 15 names, every day. A game keeps going until you lose. Which needs a fixed count and which needs a condition?
questions.a: The register is count-controlled (for); the game is condition-controlled (while).
